name: Martinair Cargo
description: White freighter with 'Martinair' in dark navy bold lettering and 'CARGO' in wider navy capitals along the forward main deck, led by three red bars forming a forward-pointing chevron just behind the forward door. The fin and the aft fuselage are red, the red's forward edge a chevron pointing forward low on the tail; two thin white chevron lines run inside it, their upper arms climbing the fin to its tip and trailing edge. White engines; the winglets white with the red chevron.

titles.style: Dark navy bold sans, capital M then lowercase (x-height about 0.78 of the capitals), right behind the chevron; 'CARGO' follows it aft.
Wider navy capitals of medium weight, smaller than 'Martinair', on its baseline aft of it.
As on the left; on the right it comes first behind the chevron, 'Martinair' aft of it, so the line reads 'Martinair CARGO' from that side.
As on the left, aft of 'CARGO'.

logos.description: Martinair's chevron: three parallel red bars bent into a '<' pointing forward, the bars' upper arms shorter and cut square at the top, the outer bar's lower arm the longest; just aft of the forward door, pointing to the nose on both sides.
The same chevron, small, near the top of the winglet's outer face.

notes: Worn by PH-MPS, a 747-412(BCF) (long upper deck: measured on shapes/B744-passenger.json, drawn for B744), Martinair's last aircraft in its own colours; the 747-400ERFs PH-CKA, PH-CKB and PH-CKC that also fly as MPH wear KLM Cargo paint (airframes/MPH.json). On PH-MPS's right side (2023-06-02, flipped) the chevron runs x 0.150-0.226, 'CARGO' 0.234-0.351 (capitals about 1.5 m) and 'Martinair' 0.363-0.557 (capitals about 2 m); the red's forward point is at x 0.751 just below the middle, with the white lines' points at 0.801 and 0.857. On the left the chevron (0.150-0.228) and the start of 'Martinair' (0.234) were read from a photo from below; the left 'CARGO' is placed by symmetry with the right side's block (it's under the wing in every left-side photo): its place is a reading, not a measurement. A small 'BOEING 747-400BCF' sits low aft and the registration with an EU flag ahead of the red: not drawn. Colours by eye. Re-measured 2026-11-20 so each white line and the red field's edge run on unbroken across the fin root: on PH-MPS each line is one straight diagonal from the fin down the body. Each edge was fitted as one straight line in metres through the fin's points and the body's (slopes 1.15-1.18 m back per m up, every point within 0.27 m), and its crossing of the fin root (3.61 m up) is the shared end point: fin x 0.3616/0.4036 and 0.6736/0.7133 at y 0 = fuselage x 0.8600/0.8672 and 0.9136/0.9205 at the crown. The red field's edge meets the crown at the fin's leading-edge foot (0.7978). Both parts' points are sampled along the straight line (fin space is sheared and the fuselage's y runs round its section, so a straight line is a curve in either space), drawn smooth. The chevrons' points are where the lines meet the lower arms as measured, within 0.25 m of the photo.
history: New in the LAX round (2026-11-20); Martinair had no scheme here before.
